sentences.text:
Heard Mr. Amiyakant Tiwari, learned counsel for the appellant in CRA No. 1008/2022, Mr. Udho Ram Koshaley, learned counsel for the appellant in CRA No. 1122/2022 and Mr. Samrath Marhas,
learned counsel for the appellant in CRA No. 1176/2022 and Ms. Madhu Nisha Singh, learned Deputy Advocate General appearing for the State/respondent on the instant applications for suspension of sentence and grant of bail (I.A. No.01 of 2022 in CRA No.1008 of 2022), (I.A. No.01 of 2022 in CRA No.1122 of 2022) and (I.A. No.01 of 2022 in CRA No.1176 of 2022).
No application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail has been filed in CRA No. 1099 of 2022 in respect of Appellant-Anil Khunte.

Learned counsel for the appellants have argued that there were two prosecutrix and the accused persons who were seven in number including the four appellants committed rape against PW-2 who is a victim-A whereas PW-4 is a victim-B and separate crimes were registered against the all seven accused persons including the four appellants and they were put to trial by the State and the trial Court with respect to victim-B (PW-4) has acquitted all the seven accused persons including the appellants from the charges.

So far as victim-A (PW-2) is concerned the evidence goes to show that she had accompanied the accused/appellants at various places and it is alleged that at that point of time, the accused committed crime against her, but medical report of the prosecutrix shows that she is a habitual to sexual intercourse and no external or internal injuries were found on the prosecutrix.
The FSL report is also negative and the authentic proof of age is also not proved by Dakhil-Kharij Register.
Counsel for the appellants submits that it is case of false implication, hence the appellants have filed the aforesaid applications for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
On the other hand, learned Deputy Government Advocate, appearing for the State/respondent opposed the prayer for grant of bail.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the records of the Court below.

Taking into account that the appellants are in jail since 08.12.2019 and hearing of these appeal would take prolonged period of time, we deem it appropriate to allow the applications for suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of appellants - Pradeep Kumar Ajay,
Dayaram Ratre and Nageshwar Patel.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the substantive jail sentence awarded to the appellants Pradeep Kumar Ajay, Dayaram Ratre and Nageshwar Patel by the learned trial Court is hereby suspended.

They shall be released on bail on their executing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Twenty Five Thousand Only) each with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for their appearance before the Registry of this Court on 22.11.2023.

They shall thereafter appear before the concerned trial Court on a date to be given by the Registry of this Court and shall continue to appear there on all such subsequent dates as are given to them by the said Court, interval being not less than 6 months, till final disposal of this appeal.
Consequently, (I.A. No.01 of 2022 in CRA No.1008 of 2022), (I.A. No.01 of 2022 in CRA No.1122 of 2022) and (I.A. No.01 of 2022 in CRA No.1176 of 2022) are allowed.

It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only confined for disposal of aforesaid IAs filed in these appeals and it shall not be construed as an expression of opinion of this Court on the merits of the matter.
List these matters for final hearing after eight weeks.

C.C. as per rules.
 Sd/- Sd/-
 (Sanjay Kumar Jaiswal) (Ramesh Sinha)
